page.layout: One printed page, right-hand side of an opening. Running head at top centre; below it a heading "IN IVLIVM II. PONTIFICEM." with a verse epigram of 3 lines in italic (opening capital G); then a rule; then a title "DE NICOTIANA FALSO Nomine Medicæa appellata." in capitals and small capitals, followed by a poem of text in italic with an initial D; "EX" at the lower right, below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: GEnva cui patrem, genitricè Græcia, partu
Pontus & vnda dedit, nobilis esse potest:
Nulla fides. In te singula solus habes.

l.i: At Medice Catharina κακοπαφμακα luesque suorum
sui, Ambitione ardens, Medicæa nomine plantam
Vtque bonis cives prius exuit, exuere herbæ
At vos auxilium qui membris quæritis ægris,
A planta cohibete manus, os claudite, & aures
Nectar enim virus fiet, Panaceaa venenum,

page.notes: Long s rendered as s throughout. The Greek word after "Catharina" reads as κακοπαφμακα in the scan; the letters are doubtful, so the Greek is marked for checking. Lines 1-3 of the first epigram are set tightly and the bottom of the page is partly obscured by the page edge; the "EX" at lower right appears to be a signature or catchword-like mark and is kept as a line. The word "Pontus" in the epigram is printed with a cut-off letter on the scan.
